invented.quote: I drive through that intersection every day.
invented.why: The brief states that the speaker lives on Alder Road, not that they drive through the intersection of Alder and 4th every day (or drive at all).

invented.quote: Right now that lot is 1.8 acres of asphalt
invented.why: The brief calls it a 1.8-acre back parking lot, not that it is paved with asphalt (as opposed to concrete, gravel, or unpaved).

invented.quote: These are people who already work here and live here, or want to: home health aides, cooks, retail workers, retirees on fixed incomes.
invented.why: The brief only states that the units will rent to households earning under 60% of the area median income, without specifying the tenants' occupations, retirement status, or local ties.

invented.quote: on land that's already paved, with no new land cleared and no one displaced.
invented.why: The brief says the project is on a back parking lot, not whether the lot is paved, whether any adjacent land must be cleared, or whether anyone is displaced.

invented.quote: so residents' cars will be on the property and not on our street.
invented.why: The brief states there are 72 parking spaces for 64 units, which does not guarantee that residents with multiple vehicles will not park on the street.

invented.quote: I'm asking you to approve it in my own neighborhood, on my own road.
invented.why: The brief says the speaker lives on Alder Road two blocks from the church and that traffic on Alder Road will increase, not that the church or project itself is located on Alder Road.

invented.quote: A slower light at Alder and 4th is a real cost
invented.why: The brief mentions the intersection at Alder and 4th dropping from a C to a D rating, not that the intersection has a traffic light.
